detail.longDescription: My git history looks like: X - Y - B - C - D (HEAD -> master) \ A (origin/master) A and B are the commits that I want to squash into one but local and remote both are diverged. I have an approach that works but is too many steps: Since branches are diverged and I don't want merge commit, I simply replay B through D on top of origin/master i.e. A using: git rebase origin/master I now have: X - Y - A - B' - C' - D' (HEAD -> master) | (origin/master) Now, squashing: git rebase -i Y pick ing, squash ing done and now: X - Y - B" - C" - D" (HEAD -> master) \ A (origin/master) Pushing the change: git push --force-with-lease And finally, got the history I want: X - Y - B" - C" - D" (HEAD -> master, origin/master) Since it involves multiple steps — it is easy to forget. I believe there is a better way of solving this? Is there a shorter solution to this?
